FloodGuard · Evidence and scenario report

Package 3385c9eacccd0d2d · generated 2026-09-23T13:25:21.4176612Z

Non-operational research demonstration. Historical observations, candidate estimates and imposed scenarios do not establish event-specific flood accuracy, actual shelter availability or observed road passability.

363 source files verified; 17 acquired dataset selections across six AOIs and eight event packages. Raw files remain outside the hosted export. Gauge observations and unresolved-rights geometries are available only in the local research package. No private agency export is required.

The original catastrophic closure of internal hospital spur 934550386 depended on its single assumed site connector. Two geometry-checked connections reduce the walking all-route loss for that same spur from 41,379.4 to 15.8 residents. Neither connector is a surveyed entrance or evidence of event-time operation.

  • This combines population from 2020, 2022 boundaries and an OSM snapshot acquired in 2026; it is not a reconstruction of event-day access.
  • Primary care, hospital care, pharmacies and shelters are distinct services. No available service substitutes for an unavailable one.
  • Walking uses an assumed 5 km/h on eligible network segments; vehicle scenarios use undirected road-class speeds. Event passability, safe connectors and turn restrictions are unverified.
  • Network speeds are varied by 0.75/1/1.25; connector times remain 5 km/h. These are sensitivity cases, not demographic mobility estimates.
  • Two baseline-demand candidates per intervention family are fixed before scenario evaluation; this is not an exhaustive optimization or a site recommendation.
  • Accepted flood-affected population, FPPS, action class, actual shelter capacity/demand and age equity remain unavailable.

Source-review findings
  • UNOSAT 3991 water extents, 13–19 September 2024: analysis_extent_asset_unavailable; public_derivative_rights_unconfirmed; observation_footprint_unavailable. Official metadata matches the September event but provides no SHP/KML/GDB download. The map is a citation, not a machine-readable or independently validated extent. Source
  • UNOSAT 4009 single-date water, 22 October 2024: not_contained_in_event_window; public_derivative_rights_unconfirmed. October 22 is outside the September event window; a near-empty October mask does not show September was dry. CC BY-SA version remains unresolved. Source
  • UNOSAT 4009 accumulated water, August–October 2024: conflicting_observation_dates; not_contained_in_event_window; public_derivative_rights_unconfirmed. Layer name ends 12 October; description and Sensor_Date end 22 October. No patch dates support a September-only extraction. CC BY-SA version remains unresolved. Preliminary product; no independent validation acceptance. Source
  • 90 source arithmetic mismatches remain recorded. Numerical children/working-age definitions and local demographic joins are not accepted. Chiang Rai 2024 age data remain missing; Pathum Thani age bands support provincial context only. Source
  • This AOI: 3 supported public name/address matches and 2 dated venue-activity reports. Neither establishes a verified routing point, continuous event operation or available capacity.
  • 291 coincident road-grade splits; 275 possible endpoint transitions require original-node/grade review. No new crossing has been inferred from proximity. Source
  • 2024-09-11: Chiang Rai PRD reported 34 people sheltered at Mae Sai municipality at 01:00 source clock on 11 September 2024. This is a reported occupancy count, not capacity. Reported use does not establish routing coordinates or available capacity. Source
  • 2024-09-14: DWF reported relief supplies delivered to the temporary shelter, donation point and kitchen at Mae Sai Mittraphap municipality on 14 September 2024. Reported use does not establish routing coordinates or available capacity. Source

Actual FPPS and action class: unavailable. Fixed-weight sensitivity range 0–100; no qualified event input is silently filled.

  • Mixed historical source dates are recorded per dataset; no common event observation timestamp.
  • Search AOIs are not administrative reporting boundaries.
  • Candidate/scenario outputs are not an official warning.
  • The preserved /studio/ satellite comparator uses transformed uncalibrated amplitude and cross-border weak-reference metrics. Those metrics do not measure Thailand-side event accuracy and are not FPPS inputs here.
  • WorldPop 2020 is modelled residential population context, not event-year counts or observed evacuation demand.
  • Demand contains positive raster cells whose centres fall in the AOI; boundary cells are not apportioned.
  • Routing uses a surrounding district/basin polygon; paths outside that polygon are not evaluated.
  • Road times use fixed class speeds on an undirected graph; one-way rules, turn restrictions and event passability are not represented.
  • Shared OSM vertex coordinates with compatible grade connect. Any additional grade transition requires recorded original shared-node evidence; geometric crossings are never noded.
  • Conservative grade separation may disconnect bridge approaches; disconnected components remain visible.
  • 100 m facility and 250 m population snaps use EPSG:32647; connector time is modelled at 5 km/h. Connector walkability and barriers are unverified.
  • OSM node, way and relation facility objects are classified separately as hospital, primary care and pharmacy. Site interior representatives are not verified entrances. Generic amenity=shelter is excluded from emergency shelter destinations and capacity.
  • No flood layer is converted into observed closures or calibrated flood probability.
  • Destination source for this scenario family is explicitly osm.
  • dataset-01 — Analysis coverage 81.0%; outside footprint unobserved. No accepted September-only reference.

    • EOS-RS Hat Yai flood proxy, 23 November 2025 v0.9: public_derivative_rights_unconfirmed; observation_footprint_unavailable. Original ZIP has 9,172 flood-proxy polygons (DN=100), WGS84, and no license or analysis footprint. Do not derive footprint from their union or bounding box. Map states roughly 30-metre likely flood pixels; lower reliability in urban and vegetated areas. Source preliminary checks use selected news/video imagery, not an independent project validation. Public map refers to an EOS legal page that failed DNS resolution. Sentinel Asia host terms forbid modification absent other permission; public derivatives remain blocked. Source
    • 90 source arithmetic mismatches remain recorded. Numerical children/working-age definitions and local demographic joins are not accepted. Chiang Rai 2024 age data remain missing; Pathum Thani age bands support provincial context only. Source
    • This AOI: 3 supported public name/address matches and 0 dated venue-activity reports. Neither establishes a verified routing point, continuous event operation or available capacity.
    • 908 coincident road-grade splits; 818 possible endpoint transitions require original-node/grade review. No new crossing has been inferred from proximity. Source

    Actual FPPS and action class: unavailable. Fixed-weight sensitivity range 0–100; no qualified event input is silently filled.

    • Mixed historical source dates are recorded per dataset; no common event observation timestamp.
    • Search AOIs are not administrative reporting boundaries.
    • Candidate/scenario outputs are not an official warning.
    • Public metadata identifies the November 11/23 Sentinel-1 pair, but original SAFE archives were not acquired. These imposed access/capacity experiments are the explicit scenario fallback, not a satellite flood candidate.
    • WorldPop 2020 is modelled residential population context, not event-year counts or observed evacuation demand.
    • Demand contains positive raster cells whose centres fall in the AOI; boundary cells are not apportioned.
    • Routing uses a surrounding district/basin polygon; paths outside that polygon are not evaluated.
    • Road times use fixed class speeds on an undirected graph; one-way rules, turn restrictions and event passability are not represented.
    • Shared OSM vertex coordinates with compatible grade connect. Any additional grade transition requires recorded original shared-node evidence; geometric crossings are never noded.
    • Conservative grade separation may disconnect bridge approaches; disconnected components remain visible.
    • 100 m facility and 250 m population snaps use EPSG:32647; connector time is modelled at 5 km/h. Connector walkability and barriers are unverified.
    • OSM node, way and relation facility objects are classified separately as hospital, primary care and pharmacy. Site interior representatives are not verified entrances. Generic amenity=shelter is excluded from emergency shelter destinations and capacity.
    • No flood layer is converted into observed closures or calibrated flood probability.
    • Destination source for this scenario family is explicitly osm.
    • dataset-05 — Station-month observations include missing measurements; absent timestamps and present null/sentinel readings are checked separately. Observation timezone remains unconfirmed.
    • dataset-10 — 2019–2025; district and sex, no age bands
    • dataset-11 — 2023–2025; village registration context
    • dataset-12 — 21 source rows at 20 distinct coordinates; identity/activation not established.
    • dataset-13 — 4 historical 2020 points within the search AOI; event availability unknown.
    • dataset-14 — 105625 valid pixels; 4 negative elevations retained for review; min/max -0.63/382.84 m.
    • dataset-15 — Version 1; generalized historical network
    • dataset-17 — 27 November 2025
    • context-admin — 9 intersecting subdistricts; 100.00% of AOI covered. Unassigned land and ambiguous memberships remain explicit.
    • context-osm — 96704 modelled edges; 564 disconnected graph components. Paths beyond the routing boundary are unevaluated. 67/67 mapped sites satisfy the 100 m connector limit; generic shelters are context only.
    • context-worldpop — 2020 modelled population 264044.87; 99.35% within 250 m. 24 nodata/invalid cells have unknown population, separate from known unsnapped demand.
    • context-destination-search — 10 km outside the demand AOI; existing OSM snapshot, points and site polygons.
    • context-sar-candidate — aoi-03_hat_yai_core: 2025-11-11T23:03:09.801147Z to 2025-11-23T23:03:09.290537Z; candidate analysis coverage is separate from Thailand reporting coverage.

      • EOS-RS Hat Yai flood proxy, 23 November 2025 v0.9: public_derivative_rights_unconfirmed; observation_footprint_unavailable. Original ZIP has 9,172 flood-proxy polygons (DN=100), WGS84, and no license or analysis footprint. Do not derive footprint from their union or bounding box. Map states roughly 30-metre likely flood pixels; lower reliability in urban and vegetated areas. Source preliminary checks use selected news/video imagery, not an independent project validation. Public map refers to an EOS legal page that failed DNS resolution. Sentinel Asia host terms forbid modification absent other permission; public derivatives remain blocked. Source

      • No accepted event flood extent is bound to this case. Any candidate-driven closures remain hypothetical; accepted flood exposure and FPPS remain unavailable.
      • The 2024 and 2025 event contexts share this same access baseline and scenario analysis. Identical values are not evidence of unchanged flood impacts. Routing stops at the selected 10 km context boundary; farther destinations and paths are not evaluated.
      • A 10 km routing buffer retains fixed AOI demand and reporting assignments. Hospital objects were source-deduplicated; operating status, entrances and event passability remain unverified.
      • This combines population from 2020, 2022 boundaries and an OSM snapshot acquired in 2026; it is not a reconstruction of event-day access.
      • Primary care, hospital care, pharmacies and shelters are distinct services. No available service substitutes for an unavailable one.
      • Walking uses an assumed 5 km/h on eligible network segments; vehicle scenarios use undirected road-class speeds. Event passability, safe connectors and turn restrictions are unverified.
      • Network speeds are varied by 0.75/1/1.25; connector times remain 5 km/h. These are sensitivity cases, not demographic mobility estimates.
      • Two baseline-demand candidates per intervention family are fixed before scenario evaluation; this is not an exhaustive optimization or a site recommendation.
      • Accepted flood-affected population, FPPS, action class, actual shelter capacity/demand and age equity remain unavailable.
      Earlier mixed-service aggregate comparator — separate assumptions

      Decision brief

      Review priority: verify consequential connections and destinations. Accepted FPPS, action class and flood-affected population remain unavailable.

      Source-review findings
      • No reviewed dated flood extent: no_reviewed_event_extent_asset.
      • 90 source arithmetic mismatches remain recorded. Numerical children/working-age definitions and local demographic joins are not accepted. Chiang Rai 2024 age data remain missing; Pathum Thani age bands support provincial context only. Source
      • This AOI: 0 supported public name/address matches and 0 dated venue-activity reports. Neither establishes a verified routing point, continuous event operation or available capacity.
      • 2975 coincident road-grade splits; 2965 possible endpoint transitions require original-node/grade review. No new crossing has been inferred from proximity. Source

      Actual FPPS and action class: unavailable. Fixed-weight sensitivity range 0–100; no qualified event input is silently filled.

      • Mixed historical source dates are recorded per dataset; no common event observation timestamp.
      • Search AOIs are not administrative reporting boundaries.
      • Candidate/scenario outputs are not an official warning.
      • The 2024 and 2025 packages reuse the same historical OSM/WorldPop context and imposed scenarios. Their event evidence inventories differ; scenario differences between observed flood years are not claimed.
      • WorldPop 2020 is modelled residential population context, not event-year counts or observed evacuation demand.
      • Demand contains positive raster cells whose centres fall in the AOI; boundary cells are not apportioned.
      • Routing uses the projected 10 km AOI buffer; paths and destinations beyond that boundary are not evaluated.
      • Road times use fixed class speeds on an undirected graph; one-way rules, turn restrictions and event passability are not represented.
      • Shared OSM vertex coordinates with compatible grade connect. Any additional grade transition requires recorded original shared-node evidence; geometric crossings are never noded.
      • Conservative grade separation may disconnect bridge approaches; disconnected components remain visible.
      • 100 m facility and 250 m population snaps use EPSG:32647; connector time is modelled at 5 km/h. Connector walkability and barriers are unverified.
      • OSM node, way and relation facility objects are classified separately as hospital, primary care and pharmacy. Site interior representatives are not verified entrances. Generic amenity=shelter is excluded from emergency shelter destinations and capacity.
      • No flood layer is converted into observed closures or calibrated flood probability.
      • Destination source for this scenario family is explicitly osm.
      • dataset-04 — Station-month observations include missing measurements; absent timestamps and present null/sentinel readings are checked separately. Observation timezone remains unconfirmed.
      • dataset-12 — 1 source rows at 1 distinct coordinates; identity/activation not established.
      • dataset-13 — 16 historical 2020 points within the search AOI; event availability unknown.
      • dataset-14 — 187489 valid pixels; 244 negative elevations retained for review; min/max -4.93/22.92 m.
      • dataset-15 — Version 1; generalized historical network
      • context-admin — 27 intersecting subdistricts; 100.00% of AOI covered. Unassigned land and ambiguous memberships remain explicit.
      • context-osm — 203139 modelled edges; 2211 disconnected graph components. Paths beyond the routing boundary are unevaluated. 274/286 mapped sites satisfy the 100 m connector limit; generic shelters are context only.
      • context-worldpop — 2020 modelled population 50467.26; 93.48% within 250 m. 59 nodata/invalid cells have unknown population, separate from known unsnapped demand.
      • context-destination-search — 10 km outside the demand AOI; existing OSM snapshot, points and site polygons.

      • No accepted event flood extent is bound to this case. Any candidate-driven closures remain hypothetical; accepted flood exposure and FPPS remain unavailable.
      • The 2024 and 2025 event contexts share this same access baseline and scenario analysis. Identical values are not evidence of unchanged flood impacts. Routing stops at the selected 10 km context boundary; farther destinations and paths are not evaluated.
      • A 10 km routing buffer retains fixed AOI demand and reporting assignments. Hospital objects were source-deduplicated; operating status, entrances and event passability remain unverified.
      • This combines population from 2020, 2022 boundaries and an OSM snapshot acquired in 2026; it is not a reconstruction of event-day access.
      • Primary care, hospital care, pharmacies and shelters are distinct services. No available service substitutes for an unavailable one.
      • Walking uses an assumed 5 km/h on eligible network segments; vehicle scenarios use undirected road-class speeds. Event passability, safe connectors and turn restrictions are unverified.
      • Network speeds are varied by 0.75/1/1.25; connector times remain 5 km/h. These are sensitivity cases, not demographic mobility estimates.
      • Two baseline-demand candidates per intervention family are fixed before scenario evaluation; this is not an exhaustive optimization or a site recommendation.
      • Accepted flood-affected population, FPPS, action class, actual shelter capacity/demand and age equity remain unavailable.
      Earlier mixed-service aggregate comparator — separate assumptions

      Decision brief

      Review priority: verify consequential connections and destinations. Accepted FPPS, action class and flood-affected population remain unavailable.

      Modelled residential population (2020): 564292.56. Access unknown because no accepted graph connector: 2702.4. These counts are not flood exposure or evacuation demand.

      Source-review findings
      • No reviewed dated flood extent: no_reviewed_event_extent_asset.
      • 90 source arithmetic mismatches remain recorded. Numerical children/working-age definitions and local demographic joins are not accepted. Chiang Rai 2024 age data remain missing; Pathum Thani age bands support provincial context only. Source
      • This AOI: 0 supported public name/address matches and 0 dated venue-activity reports. Neither establishes a verified routing point, continuous event operation or available capacity.
      • 3817 coincident road-grade splits; 3732 possible endpoint transitions require original-node/grade review. No new crossing has been inferred from proximity. Source

      Actual FPPS and action class: unavailable. Fixed-weight sensitivity range 0–100; no qualified event input is silently filled.

      • Mixed historical source dates are recorded per dataset; no common event observation timestamp.
      • Search AOIs are not administrative reporting boundaries.
      • Candidate/scenario outputs are not an official warning.
      • The 2024 and 2025 packages reuse the same historical OSM/WorldPop context and imposed scenarios. Their event evidence inventories differ; scenario differences between observed flood years are not claimed.
      • WorldPop 2020 is modelled residential population context, not event-year counts or observed evacuation demand.
      • Demand contains positive raster cells whose centres fall in the AOI; boundary cells are not apportioned.
      • Routing uses the projected 10 km AOI buffer; paths and destinations beyond that boundary are not evaluated.
      • Road times use fixed class speeds on an undirected graph; one-way rules, turn restrictions and event passability are not represented.
      • Shared OSM vertex coordinates with compatible grade connect. Any additional grade transition requires recorded original shared-node evidence; geometric crossings are never noded.
      • Conservative grade separation may disconnect bridge approaches; disconnected components remain visible.
      • 100 m facility and 250 m population snaps use EPSG:32647; connector time is modelled at 5 km/h. Connector walkability and barriers are unverified.
      • OSM node, way and relation facility objects are classified separately as hospital, primary care and pharmacy. Site interior representatives are not verified entrances. Generic amenity=shelter is excluded from emergency shelter destinations and capacity.
      • No flood layer is converted into observed closures or calibrated flood probability.
      • Destination source for this scenario family is explicitly osm.
      • dataset-03 — Station-month observations include missing measurements; absent timestamps and present null/sentinel readings are checked separately. Observation timezone remains unconfirmed.
      • dataset-09 — 2018–2024; provincial age bands
      • dataset-12 — 14 source rows at 14 distinct coordinates; identity/activation not established.
      • dataset-13 — 5 historical 2020 points within the search AOI; event availability unknown.
      • dataset-14 — 156313 valid pixels; 133 negative elevations retained for review; min/max -13.75/26.54 m.
      • dataset-15 — Version 1; generalized historical network
      • context-admin — 13 intersecting subdistricts; 100.00% of AOI covered. Unassigned land and ambiguous memberships remain explicit.
      • context-osm — 321297 modelled edges; 3340 disconnected graph components. Paths beyond the routing boundary are unevaluated. 196/239 mapped sites satisfy the 100 m connector limit; generic shelters are context only.
      • context-worldpop — 2020 modelled population 564292.56; 99.52% within 250 m. 197 nodata/invalid cells have unknown population, separate from known unsnapped demand.
      • context-destination-search — 10 km outside the demand AOI; existing OSM snapshot, points and site polygons.

      • The 2024 and 2025 event contexts share this same access baseline and scenario analysis. Identical values are not evidence of unchanged flood impacts. Routing stops at the selected 10 km context boundary; farther destinations and paths are not evaluated.

      • This combines population from 2020, 2022 boundaries and an OSM snapshot acquired in 2026; it is not a reconstruction of event-day access.
      • Primary care, hospital care, pharmacies and shelters are distinct services. No available service substitutes for an unavailable one.
      • Walking uses an assumed 5 km/h on eligible network segments; vehicle scenarios use undirected road-class speeds. Event passability, safe connectors and turn restrictions are unverified.
      • Network speeds are varied by 0.75/1/1.25; connector times remain 5 km/h. These are sensitivity cases, not demographic mobility estimates.
      • Two baseline-demand candidates per intervention family are fixed before scenario evaluation; this is not an exhaustive optimization or a site recommendation.
      • Accepted flood-affected population, FPPS, action class, actual shelter capacity/demand and age equity remain unavailable.
      Earlier mixed-service aggregate comparator — separate assumptions

      Decision brief

      Review priority: verify consequential connections and destinations. Accepted FPPS, action class and flood-affected population remain unavailable.

      Modelled residential population (2020): 564292.56. Access unknown because no accepted graph connector: 2702.4. These counts are not flood exposure or evacuation demand.

      Source-review findings
      • No reviewed dated flood extent: no_reviewed_event_extent_asset.
      • 90 source arithmetic mismatches remain recorded. Numerical children/working-age definitions and local demographic joins are not accepted. Chiang Rai 2024 age data remain missing; Pathum Thani age bands support provincial context only. Source
      • This AOI: 0 supported public name/address matches and 0 dated venue-activity reports. Neither establishes a verified routing point, continuous event operation or available capacity.
      • 3817 coincident road-grade splits; 3732 possible endpoint transitions require original-node/grade review. No new crossing has been inferred from proximity. Source

      Actual FPPS and action class: unavailable. Fixed-weight sensitivity range 0–100; no qualified event input is silently filled.

      • Mixed historical source dates are recorded per dataset; no common event observation timestamp.
      • Search AOIs are not administrative reporting boundaries.
      • Candidate/scenario outputs are not an official warning.
      • The 2024 and 2025 packages reuse the same historical OSM/WorldPop context and imposed scenarios. Their event evidence inventories differ; scenario differences between observed flood years are not claimed.
      • WorldPop 2020 is modelled residential population context, not event-year counts or observed evacuation demand.
      • Demand contains positive raster cells whose centres fall in the AOI; boundary cells are not apportioned.
      • Routing uses the projected 10 km AOI buffer; paths and destinations beyond that boundary are not evaluated.
      • Road times use fixed class speeds on an undirected graph; one-way rules, turn restrictions and event passability are not represented.
      • Shared OSM vertex coordinates with compatible grade connect. Any additional grade transition requires recorded original shared-node evidence; geometric crossings are never noded.
      • Conservative grade separation may disconnect bridge approaches; disconnected components remain visible.
      • 100 m facility and 250 m population snaps use EPSG:32647; connector time is modelled at 5 km/h. Connector walkability and barriers are unverified.
      • OSM node, way and relation facility objects are classified separately as hospital, primary care and pharmacy. Site interior representatives are not verified entrances. Generic amenity=shelter is excluded from emergency shelter destinations and capacity.
      • No flood layer is converted into observed closures or calibrated flood probability.
      • Destination source for this scenario family is explicitly osm.
      • dataset-04 — Station-month observations include missing measurements; absent timestamps and present null/sentinel readings are checked separately. Observation timezone remains unconfirmed.
      • dataset-09 — 2018–2024; provincial age bands
      • dataset-12 — 14 source rows at 14 distinct coordinates; identity/activation not established.
      • dataset-13 — 5 historical 2020 points within the search AOI; event availability unknown.
      • dataset-14 — 156313 valid pixels; 133 negative elevations retained for review; min/max -13.75/26.54 m.
      • dataset-15 — Version 1; generalized historical network
      • context-admin — 13 intersecting subdistricts; 100.00% of AOI covered. Unassigned land and ambiguous memberships remain explicit.
      • context-osm — 321297 modelled edges; 3340 disconnected graph components. Paths beyond the routing boundary are unevaluated. 196/239 mapped sites satisfy the 100 m connector limit; generic shelters are context only.
      • context-worldpop — 2020 modelled population 564292.56; 99.52% within 250 m. 197 nodata/invalid cells have unknown population, separate from known unsnapped demand.
      • context-destination-search — 10 km outside the demand AOI; existing OSM snapshot, points and site polygons.

          "No accepted event flood extent is bound to this case. Any candidate-driven closures remain hypothetical; accepted flood exposure and FPPS remain unavailable.",

          "Primary care, hospital care, pharmacies and shelters are distinct services. No available service substitutes for an unavailable one.",
          "Walking uses an assumed 5 km/h on eligible network segments; vehicle scenarios use undirected road-class speeds. Event passability, safe connectors and turn restrictions are unverified.",
          "Network speeds are varied by 0.75/1/1.25; connector times remain 5 km/h. These are sensitivity cases, not demographic mobility estimates.",
